paragraphs.source_en:
¶ 69. Title. The initial m of magnetic in A may be a majuscule. S.’s title plays on the ambiguity of ‘magnetic’,
i.e. both hypnotising and powerfully attractive; S. read Ben Jonson’s The Magnetick Lady, or Humours
Reconciled (1640) on 29 June 1818 (Mary Jnl i 216).
 1–45. S. uses double quotation marks throughout in the A text, in ll. 1, 10, 19, 28, 37 (2), 38 (2), 39, 40,
41 (2), 42, 43, 44, and 45. Ath, Medwin (1833) and 1839 have no quotation marks, but 1840 introduces
double quotation marks which nearly replicate those in A.
1. Sleep on! Sleep on! Forget thy pain: Ath, Medwin (1833), 1839. Medwin (followed by Mary in 1839)
added an extra syllable to bring the line into conformity with the poem’s metre, which in each 9-line
stanza has a syllable count of 8/6/6/8/6/8/8/8/2; but there is constant variation from this pattern (e.g.
the shortened l. 7 in this opening stanza). The MS reading was restored in 1840. Michael O’Neill notes
